baseline.note:
Subjective: 28-year-old patient presents with a 2-week history of right-sided throbbing headaches, pain rating 6/10 (worst 8/10). Photophobia noted; screens may exacerbate pain. Mild nausea without vomiting. Occasional visual aura (zigzag lines) preceding attacks. No focal neurological deficits, weakness, or numbness. No neck stiffness. Past medical history unremarkable. Family history: sister with migraines, father had stroke at age 70. Social: drinks ~3 cups coffee daily. Uses ibuprofen 400 mg ~4 days/week with partial relief.

Objective: Fundoscopic exam normal, extraocular movements intact, no motor weakness in extremities, neck range of motion normal, no meningeal signs.

Assessment: Probable migraine headache, uncomplicated.

Plan: 1) Advise migraine diary for one month (frequency, triggers, medication use). 2) Continue ibuprofen as needed; consider adding a triptan for moderate-to-severe attacks. 3) Counsel on trigger avoidance (bright light, screen time, caffeine moderation). 4) Follow-up in 4-6 weeks or sooner if symptoms change (new neurological signs, worsening pattern).
